name: Missing Consideration
consequence: A contract without consideration is void ab initio under common law.
recommended_action: Advise client to establish adequate consideration or restructure the agreement as a deed.

name: Lack of Capacity — Minor
consequence: Contracts entered into by a minor are voidable at the minor's election, except for necessaries.
recommended_action: Verify the age of contracting parties; obtain parental or guardian ratification where required.
legal_reference: Minors' Contracts Act 1987 (UK); Restatement (Second) of Contracts §14

name: Misrepresentation
consequence: A contract induced by misrepresentation is voidable and may attract damages under the Misrepresentation Act 1967.
recommended_action: Gather evidence of the false statement and its inducing effect; consider rescission and/or damages claim.
legal_reference: Misrepresentation Act 1967 s.2(1); Derry v Peek [1889] 14 App Cas 337

name: Restraint of Trade Clause
consequence: Restraint of trade clauses are prima facie void unless reasonable between the parties and in the public interest.
recommended_action: Assess geographic scope, duration, and legitimate business interest; blue-pencil if partially enforceable.

name: NDA Breach — Notification Obligation
consequence: Breach of an NDA triggers an immediate obligation to notify legal counsel and assess injunctive relief within 48 hours.
recommended_action: Notify legal counsel immediately; preserve evidence; apply for emergency injunction within 48 hours if disclosure is ongoing.
legal_reference: Coco v AN Clark (Engineers) Ltd [1969] RPC 41

name: Residual Knowledge Clause
consequence: A residuals clause may permit a recipient to use information retained in unaided memory, limiting injunctive relief.
recommended_action: Review the NDA for residuals carve-outs; advise client on scope of protection available.
legal_reference: Standard industry practice — see major cloud provider NDA templates

name: Duty of Care — Negligence
consequence: A duty of care arises where harm to the claimant was reasonably foreseeable, there is proximity, and it is fair and reasonable to impose a duty.
recommended_action: Establish the three-part Caparo test; obtain expert evidence on the standard of care applicable to the defendant.
legal_reference: Caparo Industries plc v Dickman [1990] 2 AC 605

name: Occupiers' Liability
consequence: An occupier owes a common duty of care to lawful visitors and a lower duty of humanity to trespassers.
recommended_action: Classify the claimant's status (visitor vs trespasser); review warning signs and maintenance records.
legal_reference: Occupiers' Liability Act 1957; Occupiers' Liability Act 1984

name: Defamation — Publication Requirement
consequence: A defamation claim requires proof of a false statement of fact, publication to a third party, identification of the claimant, and resulting damage.
recommended_action: Assess publication reach and seriousness threshold; consider defences of truth, honest opinion, or public interest.
legal_reference: Defamation Act 2013 s.1; Sim v Stretch [1936] 2 All ER 1237

name: Copyright Infringement
consequence: Copyright infringement occurs when a substantial part of a protected work is reproduced without licence or statutory exemption.
recommended_action: Conduct a substantial part analysis; determine if fair dealing or fair use defence applies; issue takedown or cease-and-desist.
legal_reference: Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 s.16; 17 U.S.C. §107

name: Trade Mark Infringement
consequence: Trade mark infringement requires use of an identical or similar sign for identical or similar goods/services causing a likelihood of confusion.
recommended_action: Run clearance search; assess likelihood of confusion; send cease-and-desist; consider opposition or cancellation proceedings.
legal_reference: Trade Marks Act 1994 s.10; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 9

name: Patent Claim Scope
consequence: Patent infringement is assessed against each element of the claim; prior art or lack of inventive step may invalidate the patent.
recommended_action: Obtain a claim chart; commission freedom-to-operate opinion; consider invalidity challenge if prior art exists.
legal_reference: Patents Act 1977 s.60; 35 U.S.C. §271; Actavis v Eli Lilly [2017] UKSC 48

name: Unfair Dismissal
consequence: An employee with two years' qualifying service may claim unfair dismissal; the employer must show a fair reason and follow a fair procedure.
recommended_action: Verify qualifying service period; review dismissal reason and ACAS Code of Practice compliance; advise on ET1 time limits (3 months less one day).
legal_reference: Employment Rights Act 1996 s.98; ACAS Code of Practice on Disciplinary Procedures

name: Discrimination — Protected Characteristic
consequence: Direct or indirect discrimination on a protected characteristic is unlawful; the employer bears the burden of justification once a prima facie case is established.
recommended_action: Identify the protected characteristic; gather comparator evidence; advise claimant on ACAS Early Conciliation prior to ET1.

name: Notice Period — Wrongful Dismissal
consequence: Wrongful dismissal is a common law breach of contract claim available from day one; damages are limited to the notice period remuneration.
recommended_action: Calculate correct notice entitlement; check for PILON clause; advise on bringing claim in county court or Employment Tribunal.
legal_reference: Employment Rights Act 1996 s.86; common law implied term of reasonable notice

name: Adverse Possession
consequence: A squatter may acquire title after 12 years of factual possession with the requisite intention to possess under unregistered land rules; 10 years under the LRA 2002.
recommended_action: Check Land Registry title; serve counter-notice if application received; assess whether possession has been interrupted.
legal_reference: Land Registration Act 2002 Sch. 6; Limitation Act 1980 s.15

name: Easement — Prescription
consequence: A prescriptive easement may be established by 20 years of continuous, open, and non-contentious use as of right.
recommended_action: Document historic user evidence; investigate title deeds for express grants; advise on registration requirements.
legal_reference: Prescription Act 1832; R v Oxfordshire CC ex parte Sunningwell Parish Council [2000] 1 AC 335

name: Limitation Period — General Contract
consequence: A simple contract claim becomes time-barred six years from the date of breach; specialty contracts attract a 12-year period.
recommended_action: Calculate breach date and remaining limitation window; advise client to issue proceedings or a protective claim before expiry.

name: Force Majeure Clause
consequence: Force majeure clauses are construed strictly; frustration may discharge the contract only if performance is radically different from that contracted for.
recommended_action: Review clause wording; check notification obligations; assess whether the event truly prevents (not merely hinders) performance.
legal_reference: Davis Contractors Ltd v Fareham UDC [1956] AC 696; Canary Wharf v EMA [2019] EWHC 335
